extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. It covers five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs, using realistic robotic data and in-house collection.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo; Chun-Kai Fan; Menghang Dong; Jiayu Shi; Mengdi Zhao; Bo-Wen Zhang; Cheng Chi; Jiaming Liu; Gaole Dai; Rongyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Kun Wu; Zhengping Che; Shaoxuan Xie; Guocai Yao; Zhongxia Zhao; Pengwei Wang; Guang Liu; Zhongyuan Wang; Tiejun Huang; Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: RoboBench was constructed by combining large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection, using customized workflows for each benchmark dimension that include preprocessing, annotation with VLMs, detection models or human experts, and Q&A format generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets and curated in-house collection covering manipulation settings such as single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation, with multi-view scenes, occlusion, and objects with material and physical properties.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: RoboBench uses dimension-specific annotation workflows combining VLMs/detection models and human experts. Planning annotations are generated by Gemini and refined by human annotators; scene-centric perception uses manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes; task-centric perception uses human-labeled bounding boxes; affordance frames are annotated with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances; execution-level failures are labeled by experts. Quality control includes construction-stage filtering, post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators, and majority-vote/manual review.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Two-stage quality control with data filtering during construction and post-construction validation; 20 professionally trained annotators inspected linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness; majority-vote strategy used, with easy items removed and universally failed items manually reviewed and corrected. A human study on planning data also compared automated scoring with expert judgments using Pearson correlation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 20 annotators participated in post-construction quality inspection; majority vote was used, but the exact number of labels per individual item is not specified.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were professionally trained; expert annotators with prior training were also used in the human study.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs/VLMs were used for annotation, including Gemini for structured planning annotations and video segmentation, GPT for generating functional properties/distractors, and LLMs for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit ones.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark and evaluated models have notable limitations in implicit instruction grounding, robot-view and temporal perception, long-horizon planning, object grounding, physical feasibility, and adherence to task-specific conventions. Common failure modes include missing or redundant actions, incorrect function selection, visual aliasing, parameter mismatches, wrong object references, physics violations, spatial reasoning errors, and formatting/reference errors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to guide development of more robust and generalizable embodied intelligence for robotic manipulation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is a benchmark for systematically evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains in robotic manipulation, covering instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. It is used to evaluate state-of-the-art MLLMs and compare them with text-only LLM and human references.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order); representative frames were sampled from the planning pool for affordance annotation; items all models solved correctly were removed, and items all models failed underwent manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data were built from open-source and in-house robotic data and standardized into benchmark-ready formats. Explicit instructions were rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs; frame sequences were extracted from videos as standardized inputs; planning steps were mapped into function templates; perception data were standardized into multiple-choice QA; general and task-specific filtering was applied for image quality and task validity, including excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We evaluate 14 state-of-the-art MLLMs across five embodied dimensions and uncover several critical limitations. First, models exhibit severe degradation on implicit instructions, with average scores dropping by 30%... Second, models perform poorly on robot-view recognition and temporal grounding... Third, complex planning remains the primary bottleneck

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: RoboBench thus provides a unified scaffold for measuring embodied cognition and guiding the development of more robust, generalizable embodied intelligence.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains... We evaluate several MLLMs on RoboBench, including closed-source MLLMs, open-source multi-image MLLMs, and open-source embodied MLLMs. Additionally, we introduce text-only LLM and human as reference.
